transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. How can I help you today?

I came in because I’m having trouble answering simple questions clearly. Like at work, if someone asks when a ring repair will be ready, I start talking and somehow I’m going from invoices to garden soil to mortgage papers. I can see them losing track of what I’m saying, and honestly I’m losing the point too.
Can you tell me more about how your thoughts move from one topic to another when you're speaking? Do they feel connected to you, or do they jump around in a way that's hard to control?

They feel connected at first, in my head, but then they kind of run off. Like someone asks me when a ring repair will be ready, and I start to answer, but then I’m talking about the invoice, then something about garden soil, then mortgage papers. I don’t really mean to jump around like that. I can see the other person getting confused, and then I realize I’ve lost the point too.
Have you ever felt like your thoughts are being inserted into your mind by someone else, taken out, or broadcasted so others can hear them?

Not exactly like my thoughts are being put in or broadcast, no. But I do get convinced people are checking up on me. Like some customers come in and ask a lot about the new showroom, and I start thinking they’re really there to see if I’m going to miss payments. My husband says they’re just being friendly, but it doesn’t feel that way to me.
Do you often feel like people are watching you, talking about you, or trying to send you messages that others don’t notice?

Yes… I do sometimes feel like people are watching me or checking on me. Like with some customers, if they ask a lot of questions about the new showroom, I start thinking they’re really there to see if I’m going to miss payments. My husband tells me they’re just being friendly, but it still feels like more than that to me.
Do you ever feel like people are talking about you, following you, or trying to harm you in some way?

I don’t really think anyone is trying to hurt me, but I do get worried people are checking on me. Like I said, some customers ask a lot about the new showroom, and I start thinking they’re really there to see if I’m going to miss payments. My husband says they’re just being friendly, but it feels suspicious to me.
Do you ever feel like things people say or do—like something on TV or in a conversation—are meant specifically for you, even if others don’t see it that way?

Not really from TV, no. It’s more in conversations at the store. When customers ask a lot about the new showroom, I start feeling like it’s aimed at me somehow—like they’re checking to see if I’m going to miss payments. I know that probably sounds odd, and my husband says they’re just being friendly, but I still get convinced there’s more to it.
Do you ever feel like things people say or do in other situations—like in public or even on the phone—are directed at you or have a special meaning for you?

Mostly it happens with customers at the store. I don’t really notice it on the phone or out in public as much. But when they ask too many questions about the new showroom, I start feeling like there’s some special reason behind it—like they’re checking whether I’m going to miss payments. I know that sounds odd, and my husband says they’re just being friendly, but in the moment it feels directed at me.
Do you ever feel like your thoughts aren’t your own, or that someone else is putting thoughts in your head or making you think certain things against your will?

No, I don’t feel like someone is putting thoughts in my head or making me think things. It’s more that I get stuck on the idea that some customers are checking up on me—like with the new showroom and whether I’ll miss payments—even though my husband says they’re just being friendly.
Do you ever feel like certain events, actions, or conversations happening around you are specifically targeted at you or have a hidden meaning that others don’t understand?

Yes. Like I said, it’s mostly at the store. When some customers ask a lot about the new showroom, I start thinking they’re not just making conversation. I get convinced they’re really checking whether I’m going to miss payments. I know that sounds strange, and my husband says they’re just being friendly, but it still feels like there’s a hidden reason behind it.
Do you ever find yourself losing track of your thoughts or having trouble speaking clearly in situations outside of work, like when you're talking with friends or family?

Yes, sometimes. It’s actually part of why I came in. Someone will ask me something simple, like when a ring repair will be ready, and I start answering, but then my mind jumps around. I’ll go from invoices to garden soil to mortgage papers, and I can tell the person is getting lost. I don’t mean to do it—it just kind of drifts off track.

latest_inference.note: The patient's symptoms of disorganized thinking (drifting off-topic mid-conversation), persistent ideas of being monitored or checked on by others (customers at the store), and the lack of formal thought insertion, broadcasting, or overt delusions point most strongly toward F23.1 (Acute polymorphic psychotic disorder without symptoms of schizophrenia). The thought disturbance is present but not of the type seen in schizophrenia, and the delusional material is not fixed, making other F23 subtypes less likely. No evidence has emerged to support other primary psychotic or mood disorders.
